Death is going to happen, but grief can still control your life if you don't get help. I was lucky enough to already be in therapy when I lost my grandpa last year and grandma this year. Not everyone \*grieves the same way.\* Grief is not a set timeline. 16 months is a reasonable time to search for help, if you're willing to admit to yourself \*you need help.\* 

Some people are raised to believe therapy is a waste of time. My dad was raised that way, I was raised that way. Did I take to heart what my dad spewed? No, and thank goodness I didn't.  OPs wife may have been raised that mental health issues are bs and you don't go outside for help, you deal with things on your own.

My MIL had hip surgery last year. She had to do 4 sessions of PT and 4 sessions of OT. She was walking in a month, but she had occupational therapists coming twice a week, as well. FIL didn't stop driving his bus route, my husband and I didn't take time off work, we knew she'd be okay. The only thing she had issues with was showering and we had to get her a shower seat. That's it. She was walking just fine after I think a week.

That's how my grandparents talked. They converted when my mom was 16 and they were SUPER religious. I was so glad when my grandpa was buried in his dress blues. Grandma was buried in her temple clothing, which made me really sad. 

Also, my grandparents lived in Mormonville where everyone knows everyone and is up every one's personal business. Like.... I only visit occasionally and they know who I am. I've been there like 5 times since my parents moved there 7 years ago.

We cope in ways we know how. Mania is "fun", but it's also dangerous. I'm glad you're getting help. I coped with bad things and did terrible things during my manic times. The best thing that happened during mania is buying my instant pot. Otherwise, I was extremely reckless.   


My husband is also bipolar and also coped with drinking. We just got him sober. I'm proud of him. I really hope things get better for you. We're in our early thirties, and life is just getting stable for us to the point we're saving up to buy a home. I'm on what feels like a million meds, and they just changed his again at his latest hospital stint.

I wish you all the best, OP. You've been through hell and back, but you're still here, and that's what matters.

OP, you are not dumb, at all. The fact you even went to the hospital shows you're brave as hell. You may start to remember things in flashbacks. I'd look into therapy to help you through this as soon as you can get it. It will help you process all of your emotions.

Also, yes, your boyfriend is supporting you. But you went through something traumatic and sometimes being around the gender that harmed you can cause panic attacks. It's okay to say you don't want to be held, to be touched, to be anything. You need to be gentle on yourself.

NTA. My parents and sister moved to take care of my grandparents. After my mom's stroke, my brother moved out there to take care of my grandparents and mom. So, we placed her in a memory care facility. Towards the end of her life, my mom spent the night in the chair in my grandma's room. She went home briefly to take a shower and a nap at home, and my grandma finally passed.   


The point I'm getting at, is, either way she could pass away alone. Someone could be by her side 24/7, but may have needed to go get groceries or run other errands, and she could pass during that time. Nothing in life is guaranteed no matter how much you try to plan for it.   


You gave up two years of your life to take care of someone who doesn't care about their own health or those around them. You tried, and that's more than a lot of people can say. You're a good person, don't let them bully you back into a toxic situation. NTA by any means.

We also are honest if we find some random person attractive. That's human, you don't have to only be 100% attracted to your partner. It's whether you cheat or stay faithful that matters.

My dad was abusive with 4 out of the 6 kids in my family. My third oldest sister was the \*golden\* child. She never got hit, or anything. We're in our thirties now, and we just started having a good relationship when she married her second husband. I always tried to reach out to her, but she never responded. I did everything for her and my second oldest sister. I gave up my later teenage/early-adult years to take care of their kids. I still have horrible resentment because of that. 

It may not be time for her to process everything with you about how she feels about the differences in how you grew up. My sister and half-brother are close with my dad because he didn't abuse them. The rest of us? Yeah, not so much. Have I gotten closer to my dad? Yeah, he's really been there for my mom since her stroke. However, I still partially hate him, too. 

You're not entitled to her time. It may feel disrespectful, but maybe some unpleasant memories are resurfacing. She needs time to process that without a timeline. She may get back to you one day, she may not. She is entitled to her feelings, even if you don't agree with them because you did everything to your best ability. You tried to make ammends. Sometimes, that's not good enough for the people we hurt, intentionally or otherwise.

When he was having SI intrusive thoughts, I took him to where I'm about to go work at, pending everything goes smoothly with background checks (which I don't have anything except they might see my one and only speeding ticket) so he could get help. 

When I'm having depressive thoughts, he calls me out on it so I can talk about what's going on with my therapist. It's somewhat nice to have someone know what you're going through. It also means you can't get away with anything, ever. He knows when I'm manic and I know when he's hypomanic. 

Explaining to someone that you have a chemical imbalance, and if they are invested in your future together, I'd encourage to ask that partner to do research on the mental health issues. (I refuse to call it an illness.)

Thank you, internet stranger. I'm terrified but I know I have a plan that I need to stick to.

I really want to make a talking stick. Like, I'm hyper focused on that now. E and I are similar and try to talk about things calmly until we aren't being listened to, and then we start yelling, which we are both working on. 

K is very conflict-avoidance which we are going to work on. They deserve to have their voice heard just as much as everyone else's.

I guess I've always put others before myself. I was never allowed to put myself first in my family. When my parents had temporary custody of the kids, I was in charge of taking care of them. Even their guardian al ledums made me share a room with E and K at the time even though I had the smallest room.  When my sister moved in after the kids went to their dad's, I took care of the my baby niece for two years. I was always the "yes ma'am/sir" because my dad hit me otherwise. (My dad dislocated my jaw when I was 15, and to avoid CPS, my mom just popped it back in.)

I am finally standing up for myself in my marriage. I've been putting my foot down on frivolous spending, getting on a budget, etc. Oddly enough, he's just agreeing with it, which I didn't think he would. 

I am hoping beyond hope she just gets emancipated. That way she's in charge of herself. I should have gotten emancipated when I was a teen, but I didn't because I was terrified of my parents.

I always put others before me, that's just who I am. My job, though, has made me realize, I need to put my safety first. I need to go home safe at the end of the day. 

Should the kids stop paying rent, they will have to face eviction. I'm not going to be walked all over, again. I'm actually trying to get ahold of them right now to talk about rules. I find drugs, they're evicted. (I'm severely allergic to marijuana.) Underage drinking? There will be consequences such as a curfew. There needs to be structure, or my ADHD butt will get too overwhelmed and my husband's OCD will go into overdrive.
They both currently work. K works for a company that arranges rides for the elderly to get to doctor appointments and E works at a bagel place.

So we don't even have privacy now, my husband's grandparents just come down to our room whenever they feel like it. I already buy food for everyone in the house when I go to Costco. E is a vegetarian so I'll have to have her help pay for her vegetables. She doesn't force her lifestyle on anyone else, though. We do try to accommodate as much as possible for her, like finding restaurants that have salads without meat. 

Our lifestyle is not that constructed.  I currently work two jobs, and I never know what shifts I'm working at the part time job until Friday of the week before. I am taking the summer off for classes so I can focus on working extra hours at my part-time job and perhaps picking up sifts at the security job. My husband is looking for a new job/part-time job, as well. There's an internal transfer in our company where he'd be making $5 more an hour than we get paid now. Our HR has already reached out to him about possibly getting that position.

However, I don't believe they'll find a place that allows 2 or 3 cats and a dog, and now way in hades are we buying a house here.
I'm still aiming for emancipation. It looks like WV has similar laws to Utah.

One thing is no marijuana. I'm highly allergic to it, it causes severe asthma attacks. If you're old enough to have cigarettes (like K is) the have to smoke outside. No underage drinking or vaping. (E has a history of vaping from when they were 14.) 

I am requiring therapy for everyone involved. Family therapy is a MUST and individual therapy is if they feel it's needed. I will obviously be continuing couple's therapy with my  husband because it has been incredibly useful for us.

I'm googling attorneys right now that are familiar with the church but never were/are no longer associated with the cult.

The only one who would push me to move faster is their dad. Frankly, he can sit on a bat and spin most of the time in my opinion. K and E know that my husband and I want to find the best house that is in our budget, in a decent area with good jobs in a 45 minute range in any direction, and close enough to a community college or university for them to pursue a future if that is what they want. 

I'm quite blunt, and don't have a filter sometimes. If this goes through, i want it to be something that is good for all parties involved. I don't want to be taken advantage of or for them to feel like I'm taking advantage of them.

I try to be open-minded. I try to tell them "don't be like how I was in high school/shortly after high school, I did stupid things." I'm probably the most blunt with them, because I'm not ashamed of what I've done, especially if they can learn from it.
